name: ClinuxFlowPatient
title: ClinuxFlow Patient
description: A patient's demographic record, profiling FHIR R4 Patient. Grounded against the real ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) V3 API doc (docs/NHPR SBX Doc/NHPR Doc/ABHA/ABDM_ABHA_V3_APIs_V1_31_07_2025) plus the M2/M3 milestone docs in the same folder — name/gender/birthDate/mobile/ABHA-number/ABHA-address map onto that doc's own ABHAProfile/Get-Profile field set; the KYC/verification-status extensions below map onto its §9 Get Profile / §8.6 Re-KYC / §13.7 Child-ABHA fields (see each extension's own comment for its exact source). Deliberately staff-mediated capture, not self-registration: SPEC-21 §6 already resolved that Patient never gets a login to this app ('Patient will not have a login... can see his health records via digi-locker no features more than that') — this profile constrains what Front Desk/Consultation Desk capture on a patient's behalf, not a self-service form.

element.comment: Required for real clinical use (dosing, reference ranges) even though ABHA's own KYC step doesn't strictly gate on it.
Real, practical requirement — this is the number an ABHA linkage (OTP-based) and any DigiLocker export flow both key off.
The 14-digit ABHA number, when the patient already has one (or gets one linked during this visit) — genuinely optional at capture time; a walk-in patient without ABHA yet must still be registerable.
The human-friendly ABHA address ('name@abdm'), a separate real identifier from the numeric ABHA number itself.
Narrowed from base FHIR's 0..* — one current address is what this app's own capture surfaces (Front Desk/Consultation) actually ask for.

Narrowed from base FHIR's 0..* — one emergency contact (patient_emergency_contact_name/_phone in system-patient-profile-v1.yaml, both genuinely optional there, no required: true) is what Front Desk's own capture UI asks for. All children below stay min:0 to match — this whole group is best-effort, never a hard registration requirement.

Deliberately no fixed system/use sub-constraint here, unlike Patient.telecom:mobile above — same known-deferred gap system-patient-profile-v1.yaml's own comment already flags for that slice and for identifier:abhaNumber/abhaAddress: the compiler has no mechanism to co-locate a hidden fixed value onto the same array element as the one visible field this form actually captures (patient_emergency_contact_phone -> Patient.contact.telecom.value only, no .system field exists). Requiring a fixed system here would make this element permanently unreachable, not honestly validate it.

element.short: Whether this patient's ABHA identity has completed full KYC verification
element.comment: ABHA V3 API doc §9 Get Profile's own kycVerified (boolean) — genuinely independent of verificationStatus/emailVerified/mobileVerified below: a real documented case has kycVerified:false while verificationStatus:VERIFIED (a Child ABHA verified via parent consent, not full KYC), so these are deliberately 4 separate extensions, not one collapsed flag.

ABHA V3 API doc §9's own verificationStatus (only "VERIFIED" observed directly in the doc's samples, other states implied by the field's existence but not enumerated). Naming note: §14.4.1's separate ABHA-address profile response calls the same underlying concept kycStatus instead — normalized to this one canonical field here rather than reproducing that doc-level inconsistency.

element.short: How this patient's ABHA identity was verified
element.comment: ABHA V3 API doc: AADHAAR and CHILD_ABHA confirmed directly as real verificationType values (§13.7); DRIVING_LICENCE is presumed by symmetry with the enrol/byDocument creation flow but was not directly observed as a verificationType value in the doc — no binding/ValueSet asserted here for that reason, left open (rules:'open' on the parent slicing already allows it).

element.short: Whether this patient's ABHA email was OTP-verified
element.comment: ABHA V3 API doc §14.4.1 — tracked independently of kycVerified/mobileVerified (confirmed as 3 separate booleans in that response shape, not one combined flag).

element.short: Whether this patient's ABHA mobile number was OTP-verified
element.comment: ABHA V3 API doc §14.4.1 — a real, documented reason this matters beyond just presence of Patient.telecom:mobile: ABHA's own profile.mobile field is explicitly null whenever the patient's primary mobile differs from their Aadhaar-linked mobile and hasn't separately been OTP-verified, so a captured mobile number alone doesn't imply it's verified.

element.short: This ABHA account's own lifecycle status
element.comment: ABHA V3 API doc §7.4 (login, 'list of ABHA numbers (ACTIVE and DEACTIVATED)') / §12.2 — ACTIVE or DEACTIVATED. A third, harder-terminal 'deleted' state exists via §8.3 (Delete ABHA) but is never itself returned as a status value in the doc's own samples, so it's excluded from this vocabulary rather than guessed at.

element.short: Verification channels currently usable for this patient's ABHA account
element.comment: ABHA V3 API doc's own authMethods[] (AADHAAR_OTP, AADHAAR_BIO, MOBILE_OTP, PASSWORD, DEMOGRAPHICS — varies by endpoint/account) — repeating, unlike the other ABHA extensions here, since an account can genuinely support more than one channel at once.
